source: Tax Foundation, '2026 State Tax Changes Taking Effect January 1st'

changes.GA: Georgia's flat income tax rate dropped to 5.19% on January 1, 2026 (from 5.39% in 2025), continuing a scheduled annual reduction toward an eventual 4.99%.
changes.KY: Kentucky's flat income tax rate dropped to 3.5% on January 1, 2026 (from 4% in 2025), the latest step in a multi-year triggered rate reduction.
changes.MS: Mississippi's flat income tax rate dropped to 4% on January 1, 2026 (from 4.4% in 2025), with further scheduled cuts to 3.75% in 2027 and eventually 3% by 2030.
changes.MT: Montana's top marginal rate dropped to 5.65% on January 1, 2026 (from 5.9%), with a further cut to 5.4% scheduled for 2027; the lower-bracket width was also expanded.
changes.NE: Nebraska's top marginal rate dropped sharply to 4.55% on January 1, 2026 (from 5.2%), part of a phasedown toward 3.99% by 2027.
changes.NC: North Carolina's flat income tax rate dropped to 3.99% on January 1, 2026 (from 4.25%), completing a multi-year phasedown to a flat rate.
changes.IN: Indiana's flat income tax rate dropped to 2.95% on January 1, 2026 (from 3%), with a further cut to 2.9% scheduled for January 2027.
changes.ID: Idaho's flat income tax rate dropped to 5.3% in 2025 (from 5.695%), a retroactive cut carried into the 2026 tax year.
changes.OK: Oklahoma consolidated its income tax brackets from six down to three effective January 1, 2026, and cut its top marginal rate to 4.5% (from 4.75%).
changes.OH: Ohio moved to a single flat rate of 2.75% on nonbusiness income above $26,050 as of January 1, 2026, completing its transition away from graduated brackets — though eligibility for some credits and exemptions was tightened for higher earners.
changes.SC: South Carolina's top marginal rate is temporarily reduced to 6% through June 30, 2026, and is scheduled to revert to 6.2% starting July 1, 2026.
